question: Which of the following statements can be derived from the given context and image?
model_answer:
### 1. Relevant premises from the image and context

Let:

$$
p = \text{the person in the image}
$$

Predicates:

$$
PowerTool(p) = \text{person } p \text{ is using a power tool}
$$

$$
Construction(p) = \text{person } p \text{ is engaged in a construction activity}
$$

$$
Sleeveless(p) = \text{person } p \text{ is wearing a sleeveless shirt}
$$

$$
CuttingStoneBlock(p) = \text{person } p \text{ is cutting the stone block}
$$

From the image:

$$
PowerTool(p)
$$

$$
Sleeveless(p)
$$

From the context:

$$
PowerTool(x) \Rightarrow Construction(x)
$$

This is stated as “normally indicate,” so it is a default inference unless contradicted.

Also given:

$$
Construction(p) \land Sleeveless(p) \Rightarrow CuttingStoneBlock(p)
$$

The exception about “at least one of the first and second people” working on a sculpture does not specifically establish that the image person is not doing construction.

---

### 2. Reasoning type

This uses:

- Default inference: using a power tool normally implies construction activity.
- Conjunction Introduction: combine construction activity and sleeveless shirt.
- Modus Ponens: apply the rule to derive cutting the stone block.

---

### 3. Apply the logical rules

From the image:

$$
PowerTool(p)
$$

Using the default rule:

$$
PowerTool(p) \Rightarrow Construction(p)
$$

Therefore:

$$
Construction(p)
$$

From the image:

$$
Sleeveless(p)
$$

Combine:

$$
Construction(p) \land Sleeveless(p)
$$

Apply the conditional rule:

$$
Construction(p) \land Sleeveless(p) \Rightarrow CuttingStoneBlock(p)
$$

Therefore:

$$
CuttingStoneBlock(p)
$$

So the derivable statement is:

FINAL ANSWER: D. The person is cutting the stone block.
